record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: For every space bound S(n) greater than log n, does giving a space-bounded Turing machine an auxiliary pushdown stack fail to increase its computational power? Equivalently, is the class PDM(S(n)) of languages accepted by pushdown-stack Turing machines using O(S(n)) counted work-tape space equal to DSPACE(S(n))?

evidence.quote: 6. Is PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) > logn?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S: ℕ → ℕ be a space-bound function with S(n) ≥ log n. Define DSPACE(S(n)) to be the class of languages accepted by deterministic Turing machines that, on every input of length n, use at most O(S(n)) cells of work-tape space. Define PDM(S(n)) to be the class of languages accepted by deterministic Turing machines equipped with a two-way read-only input tape, an auxiliary pushdown stack (whose contents are not counted in the space bound), and a separate counted work tape that is restricted to use O(S(n)) cells on every input of length n; the machine halts on every input.

Question: For every space bound S(n) ≥ log n, is it the case that
   PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n))?
Equivalently, does augmenting an O(S(n))-space-bounded deterministic Turing machine with an auxiliary (uncounted) pushdown stack fail to increase its computational power?
artifact.category_tag: Space complexity and auxiliary pushdown automata
artifact.status_search_result: By a classical theorem of S. A. Cook, the class of languages accepted by deterministic auxiliary pushdown machines using O(S(n)) work-tape space (S(n) ≥ log n) equals DTIME(2^{O(S(n))}). Hence PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n)) is equivalent to DSPACE(S(n)) = DTIME(2^{O(S(n))}); for S(n) = log n this is the well-known L vs. P question, which remains open. No proof of equality or separation is known for any S(n) ≥ log n.

status_evidence.title: Cook's theorem on auxiliary pushdown automata
status_evidence.snippet: AuxPDA(S(n)) = DTIME(2^{O(S(n))}) for S(n) ≥ log n (Cook 1971).
status_evidence.claim: PDM(S(n)) coincides with DTIME(2^{O(S(n))}), so equality with DSPACE(S(n)) reduces to open simulation questions such as L vs. P.

status_evidence.title: L versus P problem
status_evidence.snippet: Whether L = P is a major open problem in computational complexity.
status_evidence.claim: The S(n) = log n instance of the question is the open L = P problem.
